chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalla', from Ayub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man marries a woman, it is not permissible for him to have sexual relations with her until he gives her something worth a dirham or more, or a gift of sawiq or something else." This narration came to Al-Afdal's way; as for whether that is obligatory and leaving it is prohibited, what he narrated does not indicate that:
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for a husband to make sexual relations permissible with his wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the legal threshold for marital consummation, stipulating that intimacy is prohibited until a minimum dowry (mahr) of at least one dirham or a gift is given. It highlights the scholarly debate regarding whether this provision is an obligatory condition (wajib) for validity or a recommended practice (mustahabb), reflecting the nuanced approach of Shia jurisprudence to marital rights.
